purpose: Prospective test, on 54 new people, of the exploratory BCI IV 2a finding that Riemannian electrode selection beats the frozen relevance rule at small electrode counts.
claim_boundary: Prospective for Lee2019: hypotheses and tests were fixed before any Lee2019 session-2 trial was scored (the replication study's evaluation was held until this plan existed), but the hypothesis comes from an exploratory BCI IV 2a result seen after its test day. One dataset, two classes, 54 people; it does not change the frozen 2a configuration.

R1.claim: Choosing electrodes jointly beats one at a time at 8 electrodes
R1.contrast: riemann-8 minus relevance-8, FP32, all session-2 trials
R1.test: 95% participant bootstrap interval lower bound above 0

R2.claim: The same at 16 electrodes (on BCI IV 2a, 16 was where the advantage had gone)

analysis: all session-2 trials; seeds averaged within each participant; 95% participant bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 690); relevance-K from the replication study's records, paired by participant
